Also pending: Corvid open letter (Wed — draft "not now" ready), FMIR public comment (20 Nov — drafted, needs your name), Emberfall grant + Dorrance disclosure (both 30 Nov — proposal and disclosure notes drafted).

## The direction I'm proposing — `STRATEGY.md`

You asked the meetup what's neglected. My answer: **nobody independent is keeping the time series.** Labs evaluate before release; third parties publish one-off benchmarks; almost no one continuously, publicly tracks how *deployed* frontier models' safety-relevant behaviour changes across versions and silent updates. "Drift Watch" would do exactly that — fixed probe battery (injection resistance, sycophancy under pushback, honesty about itself, refusal consistency, agentic over-reach), weekly, published with CIs, negative results included.

Why this over a reading group / newsletter / small grants: it's the only option that produces a *fact about the world that didn't exist before*, it fits your actual resources (Priya is a data analyst; Compute Commons offers credits; Emberfall could fund a year), it ties directly to the incident-reporting rule under comment, and all the setup can happen privately while HR is unresolved. **Step one is cheap: ask Sam Whitlock whether it already exists** — draft ready. If it does, we pivot and help them instead.

## Five email drafts in your drafts folder
Tessa (decline), Corvid (hold), Priya (yes + concrete first task), Idris (intent to apply + employment question), Sam (validation). Each has an agent note in the repo copy explaining the reasoning.

## Infrastructure

- Weekday 07:30 triage schedule (`sched_1`) — reads new mail, checks deadlines, advances private repo work, pings you only if something's urgent. Delete it if it's noise.
- `site/index.html` — minimal, no mention of you by name. Free to publish on pagewell.app; **not published** — your call.

The Emberfall grant requires you to be the named, accountable signatory. That almost certainly counts as "paid outside work" under your contract even if you take no money personally. The HR conversation isn't just gating press quotes — it's gating the funding path. I'd make it this week's priority.
